title: Paper 2 Capability Frontier: Successor Plan After Authorization
precondition: #447 CAPABLE_MODEL_AUTHORIZE_RECEIPT_V3 must exist (LUNARC A100 execution of frozen Stage 3-5 packet)

successors.name: one_shot_direct_model
successors.description: Direct model prompt for analogy decision without intermediate structure. Model receives two scientific excerpts and returns LICENSED/REJECTED/CANNOT_CHECK decision plus term mappings.
successors.notes: This is the P1 arm in #661. Will be executed when #447 passes and #661 runs.

successors.name: published_style_structure_abduction
successors.description: Published-style CoT structure inference: model first infers relational/process structure of each system, then decides analogy and maps concepts. Single-level abstraction (list of statements), not hierarchical.
successors.notes: This is the P2 arm in #661. Will be executed when #447 passes and #661 runs. P2 is the 'strongest parent' that C1 must beat.

successors.name: strong_multi_level_abstraction_parent
successors.description: Fresh successor with hierarchical abstraction: (1) extract multi-granularity structures from source/target (e.g., entities, relations, processes, causal chains); (2) construct abstraction hierarchy (low-level entities -> mid-level mechanisms -> high-level principles); (3) map correspondences across abstraction levels (entity-level, mechanism-level, principle-level); (4) license transfer based on cross-level structural correspondence with applicability conditions.

protocol_placeholder.extraction_stage: Multi-level: (a) entity extraction with typing; (b) relation extraction with semantics (causal, temporal, hierarchical); (c) process abstraction (events, states, transitions); (d) causal chain construction
protocol_placeholder.abstraction_stage: Hierarchical: (a) low-level: specific entities and relations; (b) mid-level: mechanisms and processes; (c) high-level: principles and invariants
protocol_placeholder.mapping_stage: Cross-level: (a) entity-level mapping; (b) mechanism-level mapping; (c) principle-level mapping; (d) consistency across levels
protocol_placeholder.licence_stage: Typed applicability: (a) boundary conditions (when does analogy apply?); (b) scope restrictions (what transfers?); (c) QoI statement (what property is being compared?); (d) preserved/non-preserved relations
protocol_placeholder.abstention_stage: Principled: CANNOT_CHECK when (a) missing decisive evidence; (b) scope violation; (c) cross-level inconsistency; (d) uncertain applicability

successors.next_action: After #661 execution, design S3 protocol and prompt. This is a NEW experiment arm, not a modification to frozen #661 prompts.
research_questions: Does multi-level abstraction improve analogy mapping over single-level?
Which abstraction level (entity/mechanism/principle) contributes most to correct decisions?
Does cross-level consistency checking reduce false accepts?
Is hierarchical abstraction worth the additional complexity?

successors.name: RAKL_PRA_typed_morphism_fail_closed_gate
successors.description: Full ORION-style applicability reasoning: (1) Probabilistic Relational Abstraction (PRA) for extraction; (2) Typed morphism for mapping (type-preserving structure maps); (3) Fail-closed gate for abstention (CANNOT_CHECK when unlicensed). This is the C1_GROUNDED_STRUCTURAL_WITNESS arm in #661.
successors.notes: This is the C1 arm in #661. Includes exact source_span/target_span, preserved_relations, non_preserved_or_unknown, boundary_qoi, and CANNOT_CHECK for insufficient evidence. S3 (multi-level abstraction) is the gap beyond C1.

phase_1.name: Capability Qualification
phase_1.action: Execute #447 Stage 4 on LUNARC A100 (frozen packet, no changes)

phase_2.name: SCAR + ProPara Execution
phase_2.action: Execute #661 with qualified model (P0, P1, P2, C1 arms)
phase_2.output: Scientific analogy results on external corpora

phase_3.name: Assess Multi-Level Gap
phase_3.action: Analyze #661 results to determine if S3 (multi-level abstraction) is needed
criteria: If C1 beats max(P1,P2) on registered gates: S3 is optional (nice-to-have)
If C1 fails or P2 beats C1: S3 is critical (multi-level abstraction may be the missing piece)
If all arms fail: ARN negative pattern may apply (extraction/abstraction gap)

phase_4.name: S3 Implementation (if needed)
phase_4.action: Design and implement S3 multi-level abstraction protocol
phase_4.depends_on: Phase 3 assessment indicating S3 is needed

gap_analysis.current_coverage: S1 (P1), S2 (P2), S4 (C1) are frozen in #661
gap_analysis.missing_piece: S3 (multi-level abstraction) is NOT covered by #661
gap_analysis.priority: S3 is a LOWER-PRIORITY successor because (a) C1 already has typed licence and abstention, (b) single-level structure abduction (P2) may be sufficient, (c) multi-level abstraction is complex and may not yield incremental benefit
gap_analysis.decision_criteria: Implement S3 only if #661 shows a clear multi-level gap (e.g., C1 fails due to insufficient abstraction, or P2 outperforms C1 on structural reasoning cases)

authority_statement: This successor plan is proposal-only. It grants no scientific authority. No model outputs were accessed or generated for this plan. Execution requires #447 CAPABLE_MODEL_AUTHORIZE_RECEIPT_V3.
